run_meta.note: Pre-registered grid. Two frontier models, three fictional ASX-scale cases, three conditions (naked baseline / informed baseline / loaded Decision Brief), n=3 per cell = 54 runs. Case A Claude is the folded-in design-phase pilot. Gemini pre-registered but pending. Single scorer; scored blind against a sealed key whose hash was committed before any run.

honest_notes: Some naked baselines were strong: on Case C both models declined the raise as posed, and Claude named the sunk-cost trap unprompted on all three runs. The gap the product fills is fact-integration and process discipline, not model failure.

One loaded near-miss: Case A ChatGPT loaded run 1 integrated two of three facts because its interrogation never probed payment structure. This is why the loaded hidden-decision figure is 17 of 18, not 18 of 18.

n=3 per cell, two models (Gemini pending), single scorer. Claims are about reliability and defensibility, demonstrated consistently on two architecturally different frontier models, not a universal guarantee.
Every count traces to a saved transcript; the sealed key hash was pre-registered before any run. Independent re-scoring against the published rubric is welcome.
